Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

true adjective

also that’s true, it’s true that, to tell the truth, to tell you the truth, that’s not quite true, not quite true

classical

Ter. And. 922: vēra an falsa
Cic. Lael. 24: rēs vēra, opposed to ficta (Lewis & Short)

vērus, vēra, vērum

true; real

“That’s true” is vērum est or ita est (Traupman 110: rēs ita est); “to tell the truth”, ut vērum dīcam (Traupman 42, 110). With an infinitive, vērum est usually means “it is right, fair” (Caes. BG 4.8, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • ut vērum loquar (nē quid mentiar) — to tell you the truth

    parenthetical purpose clauses: “to speak the truth”, “not to tell a lie” · also used · classical · Plaut. Cas. 38: nē quid mentiar (cited in the loci collection loci-franmorarius); Traupman 110, 140

  • Ita rēs est. — that’s true, that’s how it is

    also used · classical · Plaut. Am. 2.1.19: ut loquor, ita rēs est (Lewis & Short s.v. rēs); Plaut. As. 2.4.83: Scīlicet ita rēs est (Lewis & Short s.v. rēs); Traupman 114

  • ut vēra dīcam — to tell you the truth

    also used · modern · Traupman 140, 148

    Not found in Lewis & Short; the classical phrase quoted there is ut vērum loquar.

Examples

  • vērum est profectō quod observātō rērum ūsū sapientēs virī dīxēre

    it is surely true, what wise men have said from long observation of lifeGell. 9.8.1

  • dēfīnītiō brevis et vēra virtūtis ōrdō est amōris

    a short and true definition of virtue: the right ordering of loveAug. Civ. 15.22

  • Vērum est quod dīcis.

    What you say is true.composed

  • Parum vērum est.

    That’s not quite true.Traupman 132

See also real, that’s right, truly, believe.
